**sqlpipe Architecture Overview**

sqlpipe is a streaming pipeline that moves data from PostgreSQL to S3 in Parquet format through three concurrent stages connected by bounded channels.

The **Reader** opens a server-side cursor against PostgreSQL and fetches rows in configurable batches. Each batch is serialized into an in-memory buffer and pushed onto a channel, applying backpressure when the converter falls behind.

The **Converter** consumes row batches, maps PostgreSQL types to Parquet logical types, and assembles them into Parquet row groups. It handles schema inference or accepts a explicit schema, encoding each row group with the configured compression (Snappy, Zstd, etc.) before forwarding the finished byte buffer downstream.

The **Uploader** initiates an S3 multipart upload, writing each row group as a part. It retries individual part uploads with exponential backoff. On completion it finalizes the multipart upload; on failure it aborts, preventing orphaned parts.
